title: The audit is done. What happens to the audit recommendations?
meta_title: Audit Recommendations for Care Services | CareStreamAI
meta_description: Finished an audit and not sure what next? CareStream drafts audit recommendations and an action plan. You edit it, set owners and approve it.
lede: A finished audit gives you a score. It does not give you a list of jobs with names against them. On the paid plans, CareStream turns the answers into audit recommendations you can read, change and approve. Audits themselves are free, and you can see how training built from your own policies fits alongside them.

intro.heading: The audit is signed. The jobs are still on a scrap of paper.
intro.sub: A scenario we see in many care settings.
intro.paragraph: A senior carer completes the monthly infection control audit on a tablet. Every question is answered, photos are attached and the report is saved. The manager reads it that afternoon and sees eleven answers marked as failed. She jots a few jobs on a pad and goes back to the floor. A week later nobody can say who was meant to replace the sluice room bin. A month later the same question fails again. The score is on file, but the follow through is not. Here is how that plays out.

trail.text: A senior carer completes the monthly infection control audit on a tablet.
Every question is answered, photos are attached and the audit is signed.
The report is saved, with a score for each section.
Eleven answers failed. The manager scribbles a few jobs on a pad.
Who was meant to replace the sluice room bin? Nobody wrote a name.
The same question fails again, and nobody notices the pattern.
A score and a pad. No owner, no date, no proof of a fix.
“You found this in March. What did you do about it?”

trail_close: The audit itself is not the problem. The gap is between the findings and the fix. Here is how CareStream helps you close it, with you making every decision.

why.heading: A score tells you what failed, not who will fix it
why.sub: Finding a problem is half the job. The other half is showing it was dealt with.

cards.title: Notes on a pad get lost
cards.body: Jobs written in a hurry have no owner and no date. By the following week, half of them have slipped out of everyone's mind.

cards.title: Writing the plan takes time
cards.body: Turning sixty answers into a clear audit action plan is a job for a quiet hour. Most managers do not have one, so the plan stays unwritten.

cards.title: Repeat failures hide in plain sight
cards.body: If the same question fails month after month, that is a finding in itself. It is hard to spot when each report sits in its own file.

talk.heading: The questions managers ask, and how CareStream answers them
talk.sub: Read this as a conversation. The questions are the ones we hear most.

items.q: We already complete audits. What would CareStream add?
items.a: If you already use an audit tool, you know the hard part is what comes after. CareStream scores the audit, saves the audit report, and on paid plans drafts audit recommendations and an action plan you edit. Then it tracks who does each job and checks it at the next audit.

Yes. More than 100 audits are free on every plan, including the Free plan. You get scoring, photos, signatures, the PDF audit report, scheduling and manual actions. The drafted suggestions and action plan are on paid plans.

items.q: How does it come up with the recommendations?
items.a: When an audit is completed, our own machine learning reads the answers and evidence and drafts up to 12 suggested actions. Each is marked immediate, priority or monitor. It is a starting point, written for you to read, not a finished decision.

Yes. A machine drafted suggestion can miss context that you know and it does not. That is why the plan starts as a draft. You read every line, edit or delete what does not fit, and only then approve it.

items.q: What happens after I approve the plan?
items.a: Everyone named in it is emailed. Owners see their jobs in the Staff Hub under My actions, mark progress, add a note and attach up to 10 photos. If someone needs longer, they ask with a reason and an admin decides.

items.q: How do I know the fix worked?
items.a: At the next audit of the same kind, the earlier actions are listed. The auditor marks each as fixed or not fixed. If it is not fixed, the action reopens and the owner is emailed. Nothing is closed just because someone said so.

items.q: Does it tell me my CQC rating?
items.a: No. The scores are CareStream's own, they are not a CQC rating, and an audit is not a record sent to the regulator. What you get is a clear, dated record of what you found, what you decided and what you checked.

items.q: What does it cost, and can I try it?
items.a: You can create a free account and run audits straight away. Paid plans come with a 14 day free trial, which is where recommendations and the drafted plan are included. See the pricing page for plan details.

limits.heading: A way to organise your response, not a replacement for your judgement

cards.title: Suggestions can be wrong
cards.body: Drafted suggestions come from our own machine learning. They can miss local context. You decide what is right for your service, and nothing is assigned until you approve.

cards.title: Recommendations are on paid plans only
cards.body: The drafted recommendations and action plan start on Starter. On the Free plan the audit still runs and scores, and you can add and track your own audit actions by hand.

cards.title: It is not a regulator record or a rating
cards.body: Audit scores are CareStream's own and are not a CQC rating. Audits are not submitted to the regulator. They are your own evidence that you looked, acted and checked.

items.a: They are suggested next steps drawn from the answers in a completed audit. In CareStream they are drafted for you on paid plans, so you start from a list instead of a blank page.

items.q: What is an audit action plan?
items.a: It is the list of jobs that follow an audit, each with an owner, a due date and a priority. CareStream drafts up to 12 actions, you edit them, and the plan only takes effect when you approve it.
You choose. An owner can be a member of staff or an outside contractor. Staff see their actions in the Staff Hub, and admins track the ones given to contractors.

items.q: Can I add my own actions without the drafted plan?
items.a: Yes. Manual actions are on every plan, including Free. You can add an action, give it an owner and date, attach photos and close it out, with no drafted recommendations needed.

groups.group: About the audit tool and the audit report

items.q: Is CareStream a free audit tool?
items.a: Running audits is free on every plan. You get a library of more than 100 audits, scoring, photos and signatures. The audit library lists them by care service.

items.q: What is in the audit report?
items.a: A branded PDF with the overall and section scores, each answer, photos, a summary, the action plan with outcomes and re-check results, and signatures. It is saved against the audit and emailed to admins.

items.q: Do I need a manager to approve an audit?
items.a: Only if you want it. Manager approval is optional and off by default. When it is on, a completed audit goes to your registered or care manager, who approves it or sends it back.

items.q: Can an audit lead to staff training?
items.a: Yes. You can link an audit to the free CPD courses or to your own training modules, and the completed audit offers them. For example, an infection control audit can point to the infection prevention and control course. See also adhoc training.

guide.heading: A practical way to turn audit findings into action
guide.lede: A good audit is only useful if something changes afterwards. This is a simple way to move from a finished audit to a fix you can show, whatever audit tool you use.

sections.h3: What a clear audit action plan needs
paragraphs: Providers of regulated activities must have systems to assess, monitor and improve the quality and safety of the services they provide. An audit is one way to assess. The action plan is how you show you then improved.

Under regulation 12, care and treatment must be provided in a safe way, which includes assessing and mitigating risks. A fix with an owner, a date and a photo is much easier to stand behind than a line in a meeting note.

checklist: Within two days: read the report and the failed answers, and decide what is urgent.
Within a week: approve an audit action plan where every action has one owner and one due date.
As actions close: ask for a photo or a short note, so the record shows what was done.
At the next audit: check each earlier action is fixed, and look for any question that fails twice.

paragraphs: Treat drafted suggestions as a colleague's first pass. Check each one against what you know about your building, your residents and your staff. Remove anything that does not apply, and add anything the draft missed. The decision, and the responsibility, stays with you.

guide.note: For the inspector. Keep the report, the approved plan and the re-check result together. They show what you found, what you decided and whether it worked.
